chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When you prostrate, say the Takbir and say: 'O Allah, to You I have prostrated, and by You I have believed, and to You I have submitted, and upon You I have relied, and You are my Lord. My face has prostrated to the One who created it and cleaved its hearing and sight. All praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds. Blessed is Allah, the best of creators.'
Then say: 'Glorious is my Lord, the Most High, and by His praise,' three times.

So when you raise your head, say between the two prostrations: 'O Allah, forgive me, have mercy on me, deliver me, and ward off [evil] from me. Indeed, I am poor in need of whatever good You send down to me. Blessed is Allah, Lord of the worlds.'

key_terms.سُبْحَانَ رَبِّيَ الْأَعْلَى: Glorious is my Lord, the Most High

ai.seo_question: What are the recommended supplications to recite during prostration in Islamic prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) provides the canonical formula for the supplication of prostration (sajdah) and the interval between prostrations (bayn as-sajdattayn), rooted in the Shia tradition of reciting specific phrases before the general glorification. It highlights the theological emphasis on total submission (islam) and reliance (tawakkul) upon the Creator, linking the physical act of bowing to the spiritual acknowledgment of God as the 'Best of Creators' (Ahsan al-Khaliqin).

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad Bin Usman, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘When you perform Sajdah, so exclaim a Takbīr and say, ‘O Allahazwj! To Youazwj I perform Sajdah, and in Youazwj I believe, and to Youazwj I submit, and upon Youazwj I rely, and Youazwj are my Lordazwj. My face perform Sajdahs to the Oneazwj Who Created it, and Cleaved its hearing and its vision. The Praise is for Allahazwj, Lordazwj of the worlds. Blessed is Allahazwj, the best of the creators’.
Then say, Glorious is my Lord<sup>azwj</sup> the Exalted and by His<sup>azwj</sup> Praise’ – three times.

So when you raise your head, say in between the two Sajdah, ‘O Allahazwj! Forgive me, and be Merciful to me, and Recompense me, and Defend me [28:24] Surely I stand in need of whatever good You may Send down upon me. Blessed is Allahazwj, Lordazwj of the worlds’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad ibn ‘Uthman from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “Abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

when you bow down for sajdah say, ‘Allah is great. then say, ‘ 0 Lord, I have bowed down to prostrate before You, I believe in You, submitted myself to You, have appealed to You to be my attorney and You are my Lord. My face has prostrated before the One who has created it, who has cut out for it a hearing means and a seeing means (ears and eyes). All praise belongs to Allah, the Lord of the worlds. Allah is most Blessed and the best Creator.
Then say, ‘My Lord, the most High, is free of all defects. three times.

While sitting straight between the two prostrations, say, ‘O Lord, forgive me, grant me mercy, grant me protection, and defend me against my enemies. I am in great need of the good that You have sent to me. Blessed is Allah, Lord of the worlds.”
